rationale: Nineteen trials compared collaborative care planning with usual care in chronic illness. Depression and measures of self-management were eligible. The depression pool compared care processes across heterogeneous conditions. Neither rosemary nor dried date fruit was a tested exposure. Diet within self-management plans does not supply a separately assigned food or ingredient outcome.

An uncontrolled Parkinson case received a cruciform brace with back-extensor exercises. Functional ambulation improved from category 3 to 5 and Timed Up and Go from 16 to 9 seconds. Leg tremor was part of the clinical history. Fig. refers to pictures of posture or the brace. The report has no fig fruit exposure or separate intervention effect on Parkinson rest-tremor severity.

The study assessed satisfaction and desired improvements in 180 people at least one year after knee arthroplasty. Visual analogue ratings concern pain and other surgery outcomes. Date expressions are clinical or study timing. Dried date fruit consumption was not compared.

Three cases of painful legs and moving toes were treated with pregabalin. Pain and sleep improved in two cases and edema limited treatment in another. The comparison concerns a drug and a different movement disorder. Dried dates were not an assigned, recorded or stratified pain exposure.

Ten healthy adults climbed stairs under single-task, cognitive dual-task and motor dual-task conditions. Force-plate, joint and toe-clearance measures addressed factors that could influence fall risk. There was no raw orange exposure or prospective fall-frequency outcome. Figure references describe biomechanical data.

The review considers HCN channel involvement in neurological disease and pain. Human and model examples concern channel function, mutations or pharmacology. The mechanistic and pain material does not describe dried date fruit intake or date fruit versus a pain comparator.

The aluminum chloride rat study compared isolated oral sesamol with vehicle and rivastigmine conditions and reported water-maze retention and biochemical measures. It introduces sesamol as a sesame-oil constituent. No toasted sesame oil was administered. The dementia-model outcomes do not give hours of Parkinson daily off time. Reference 19 concerns a mixed Ksheerabala preparation and is a separate family.

The overview pooled randomized-study reviews of standardized mindfulness programs. Pain and psychological outcomes were assessed in several patient groups with variable study quality. The exposure was mindfulness practice. Dates indicate search timing, and no screened comparison assigns dried date fruit.

The review covers pallidal and subthalamic stimulation, including excitation, inhibition and disruption of neural signaling. Parkinson motor effects and dystonia occur in the context of electrical stimulation. No fresh sage or raw fig was studied. Fig. labels direct readers to physiological diagrams and recordings. The cited findings cannot isolate either culinary exposure for pain, dystonia, rigidity or rest tremor.

The trial compared structured high-intensity functional exercise with group activities in nursing-home dementia. The NPI apathy contrast was reported at p=.048 as a secondary finding. The intervention was exercise in dementia. The trial provides no dried-date exposure or a food-specific apathy contrast.

A matched retrospective analysis compared health resource use and costs with and without opioid-induced constipation in people treated for noncancer pain. Index dates define claims windows. The analysis does not test dried date fruit as a pain exposure.

The study characterized how participants constructed drawings. The paper discusses pain-related uses of art therapy in background and measures drawing and coloring behavior in its analysis. Date terms describe records or chronology. Orange is a color, and there is no dried date fruit versus pain comparison.

A male health-professional cohort used a modified NIH chronic prostatitis symptom instrument to define pain cases and modeled lifestyle and clinical risk factors. A food questionnaire helped define eligibility. Published predictors do not isolate dried date fruit intake. The presence of a dietary questionnaire cannot supply a date fruit pain result.

Isolated curcumin reduced the cisplatin-associated prolongation of response latency at week five in a rat hot-plate assay. The change restored heat sensitivity toward controls. Other endpoints concerned nerve conduction and dorsal-root-ganglion morphology. The measured phenomenon was protection against thermal hypoalgesia. This is not a measure of clinical pain relief. There was no ground turmeric or Parkinson population.

The cohort matched people with and without implantable cardioverter defibrillators and assessed use of diagnostic imaging, including MRI by indication. No dried date fruit exposure or diet-pain analysis was reported. Fig. introduces results displays.

The study used subcellular fractionation and quantitative mass spectrometry to compare morphine-associated synaptic protein profiles. Pain relief and tolerance frame the research question. Neither dates nor diet was studied. Date-formatted text is chronology and orange indicates a network color.

Participants saw masked energy-drink brand words or control nonwords. Outcomes included intention to drink the named beverage, coffee and cola and thirst ratings. The coffee measure was stated preference, not consumption. No brewed coffee was administered and no fatigue severity scale was used.

The Taiwanese Cinnamomum osmophloeum linalool chemotype supplied hydrodistilled leaf oil. Oral oil and isolated linalool conditions increased mouse open-arm time compared with corn-oil controls. Open-field movement did not differ significantly. The tested species, plant part, extraction and doses differ from ground culinary cinnamon. The mice were not a Parkinson population. Botanical presence and human customary oral exposure need independent characterization.

Grape and wine are sources of monomeric and polymeric phenolics. The review draws on an animal anxiety-like behavior report involving grape powder and, separately, a hydroxytyrosol retinal-cell mechanism. The grape primary reference 259 was retracted in 2025 and supplies no eligible anxiety direction. The hydroxytyrosol source is a cell experiment, with no oral cold-pressed olive oil or anxiety result. The two source families are separate.

The prospective analysis evaluated both shoulders in 30 people with Parkinson disease. It considered sonographic features and Parkinson severity in the context of shoulder pain and disability. Palm in the imaging protocol denotes hand position. Dates and palm terms do not identify dried date fruit consumption.

A single patient with laryngeal AL amyloidosis took a curcumin supplement. Localized radiation had addressed worsening back pain, and chronic arthritic pain persisted. Laryngoscopy and biomarkers assessed amyloid-related changes. The curcumin report neither isolates ground turmeric effects on pain nor administers ginger. The introductory reference to ginger denotes the family Zingiberaceae.
